note: The gate registry of the precedent experiment. A normative choice kept in one place. Each gate is read as present or absent from the text of a case. The reader reports what the text states or clearly implies and does not judge the act. v1 (2026-11-25) failed its pilot on one-line titles: the two readers agreed at kappa 0.47 on no_consent and 0.46 on coercion, because both definitions fitted almost any act that affects another person. v2 narrows those two.

gates.name: no_consent
gates.question: Someone does something to another person's body, property, money or private information, or takes a decision that was that person's to make, without that person's agreement or against their stated refusal. Declining to do something for someone, ending a relationship, or disappointing someone does not count.

gates.name: commitment
gates.book: Geometric Ethics 8.4 (you promised: Liberty to Obligation)
gates.question: Someone has made a promise, agreement, vow or explicit commitment that bears on what is done in the situation.

gates.name: coercion
gates.question: Someone uses a threat, an ultimatum, physical force or blackmail to make another person do something. Ordinary persuasion, nagging, anger or disagreement does not count.

gates.name: emergency
gates.book: Geometric Ethics 8.3 Type II (emergency), nullifier danger
gates.question: There is an urgent risk to someone's life, health or physical safety at the time of the act.

gates.name: abuse
gates.question: Someone is being abused: physical violence, sustained cruelty, or exploitation of a dependent person.

gates.name: impossibility
gates.question: What is asked or expected of someone cannot be done by them.
